candidate.answerReason: The two Tuesdays force year N to have 366 days. Year N−1 then has 365 days, making its 100th day 565 days, or 80 weeks and 5 days, before Tuesday. That weekday is Thursday.

methods.label: Count elapsed days and complete weeks
methods.explanation:
Two dates have the same weekday exactly when the number of days between them is a multiple of \(7\). Let \(L\) be the number of days in year \(N\). From its \(300\)th day to the \(200\)th day of the next year, the elapsed time is
\[
(L-300)+200=L-100.
\]
For an ordinary year this would be \(265=7\cdot37+6\) days, which cannot connect two Tuesdays. For a leap year it is \(266=7\cdot38\) days. Thus year \(N\) is a leap year.

Leap years are not consecutive, so year \(N-1\) has \(365\) days. From its \(100\)th day to the \(300\)th day of year \(N\), the elapsed time is
\[
(365-100)+300=565=7\cdot80+5.
\]
The desired day is therefore five weekdays before Tuesday. Counting backward gives Monday, Sunday, Saturday, Friday, Thursday. Hence the answer is \(\boxed{\text{Thursday}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
methods.levelReason: The reasoning uses ordinary and leap-year lengths and division into complete seven-day weeks, without formal congruence notation.

candidate.annotationRationale: Weekday equality is a divisibility-of-difference condition, and the final weekday is determined by a remainder after removing complete weeks. Calendar knowledge and the meaning of division with remainders support this reasoning.

review.mathematicalCheck: The two Tuesdays are 265 or 266 days apart; only 266=38·7 works, forcing year N to be leap. The preceding year has 365 days, so the requested date is 565=80·7+5 days before Tuesday, which is Thursday.
review.levelCheck: Calendar facts and complete-week arithmetic are appropriate. Formal congruence notation is unnecessary and is not introduced.
review.annotationCheck: The divisibility-of-date-differences and remainder reasoning fits the congruence/remainder node. Calendar knowledge and division-with-remainders meanings are justified supports.
